blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: An audit proxy's handler is `(proxy, method, args) -> { audit(method); return method.invoke(target, args); }`. The target's class does not override equals. A session stores the proxy in a field `current`. On logout it runs `if (current.equals(handle)) close();`, where `handle` holds the very same proxy reference. What happens?

options.text: close() runs, since equals on a proxy is Object's own equals, which bypasses the handler
options.says: the proxy sends equals, hashCode and toString to invoke like any interface method

options.text: close() runs, since the target gets the call and treats the proxy that wraps it as itself
options.says: the target's equals knows nothing of the proxy: Object's equals compares references, and the proxy is a different object

options.text: close() is skipped, since the target gets the call and the proxy is a different object from it
options.says: equals reaches invoke, the handler asks the target, and the target is a different object from the proxy, so it answers false

options.text: close() is skipped, since Proxy answers equals itself by comparing the handlers of the two proxies
options.says: Proxy answers no Object method itself; it sends equals to the handler, which here asks the target

origin.section: equals, hashCode and toString Reach the Handler Too, So the Handler Decides the Proxy's Identity

questions.stem: A metrics handler is `try { return method.invoke(target, args); } finally { record(method); }`. The interface method `String load(String id)` declares no exceptions, and the target throws NoSuchElementException for an unknown id. The caller wraps the call in `catch (NoSuchElementException e)`. What does the caller get for an unknown id?

options.text: Its catch block runs, since an unchecked exception from the target passes through the proxy unchanged
options.says: it would, if the handler threw it; but the handler throws what method.invoke threw, the checked InvocationTargetException

options.text: Its catch block runs, since method.invoke throws whatever the target threw, and the handler lets it go
options.says: method.invoke wraps whatever the target throws in an InvocationTargetException

options.text: An UndeclaredThrowableException, since method.invoke wrapped it in a checked exception that load does not declare
options.says: the handler lets the InvocationTargetException out, and a checked exception the method doesn't declare reaches the caller wrapped in UndeclaredThrowableException

options.text: An UndeclaredThrowableException, since the proxy wraps any exception a handler throws, checked or unchecked
options.says: an unchecked exception thrown by a handler passes through unchanged; only undeclared checked ones are wrapped

origin.section: Method.invoke Wraps Whatever the Target Throws, So the Handler Must Unwrap It

questions.stem: A rate-limiting handler throws `new java.util.concurrent.TimeoutException("budget spent")` (a checked exception) when a client has used up its calls. The interface method is `byte[] fetch(URI uri) throws IOException`, and the caller is `try { client.fetch(uri); } catch (IOException e) { useCache(); } catch (RuntimeException e) { fail(e); }`. What happens when the budget is spent?

options.text: Neither block runs, since the TimeoutException leaves fetch as itself, a checked exception the caller did not catch
options.says: the proxy checks what the handler throws against fetch's throws clause and wraps an undeclared checked exception

options.text: Neither block runs, since the handler does not compile: invoke may only throw what the interface methods declare
options.says: invoke is declared throws Throwable, so the compiler accepts any exception from a handler

options.text: The RuntimeException block runs, since the proxy wraps the exception in an UndeclaredThrowableException
options.says: TimeoutException is checked and fetch doesn't declare it, so the caller gets an UndeclaredThrowableException, which is unchecked

options.text: The IOException block runs, since the proxy turns the exception into the type that fetch declares
options.says: the proxy never converts an exception to a declared type; an undeclared checked exception becomes UndeclaredThrowableException

origin.section: A Checked Exception the Interface Method Doesn't Declare Reaches the Caller as UndeclaredThrowableException

questions.stem: A caching proxy keeps the result of each interface method marked `@Cached`. In the report service, `summary()` is not marked and calls `totals()`, which is marked; `totals()` takes no arguments. A dashboard calls `summary()` on the proxy ten times. How many times does the body of `totals()` run?

options.text: Once, since totals() is marked and the handler caches every call made to it
options.says: the handler only sees calls made on the proxy; summary calls totals on the target itself

options.text: Once, since the target's own calls go back through the proxy that was built around it
options.says: inside the target, totals() means this.totals(), and this is the target, not the proxy

options.text: Ten times, since the call to totals() is made on the target and never reaches the handler
options.says: the proxy saw only summary(), which isn't marked; the call on this goes straight to the target's method

options.text: Ten times, since the handler sees totals() but leaves out calls that start inside the target
options.says: the handler never sees the call at all: a call on this does not pass through the proxy

origin.section: A Call the Target Makes on this Never Reaches the Proxy

questions.stem: A container replaces each `CardGateway` bean with a java.lang.reflect.Proxy over it. One old class still does `((AcmeCardGateway) gateway).webhookSecret()`, where `AcmeCardGateway` is the bean's class. What happens on that line?

options.text: It works, since the generated proxy class extends AcmeCardGateway and inherits webhookSecret()
options.says: Proxy generates a class that implements the listed interfaces only; it can't extend a class

options.text: It works, since the generated proxy class copies every public method of the object it wraps
options.says: the generated class has only the methods of the listed interfaces, and it is no AcmeCardGateway, so the cast fails before any call

options.text: It throws ClassCastException, since the generated proxy class has no AcmeCardGateway supertype
options.says: the proxy is an instance of a generated class that implements only the listed interfaces, so it is no AcmeCardGateway

options.text: It throws ClassCastException, since the proxy class is generated at run time, after the cast was compiled
options.says: the cast is checked at run time against the proxy's actual class; it fails because that class does not extend AcmeCardGateway, not because it was generated late

origin.section: One InvocationHandler Receives Every Call on Every Method of the Proxied Interfaces

concepts: A JDK proxy implements only the listed interfaces: it is not an instance of the target's class, so a cast to that class fails, and Proxy refuses a class; proxying a class needs a generated subclass.
